research_question: Do epitope labels exhibit stronger same-chain spatial autocorrelation than sequence-local autocorrelation, and which preregistered spatial scale is most defensible for an exploratory multi-relation encoder?
primary_hypothesis: At 8 Angstrom, the mean positive-neighbor lift is greater than one and the validation-complex macro leave-one-out neighbor-label AUPRC is higher than for an eight-residue sequence window.
registered_strata: antigen length below 200, 200 to 500, and above 500 residues
epitope prevalence at most 0.05 versus above 0.05
one versus multiple positive spatial components at 8 Angstrom

statistics.primary_comparison: within-complex spatial_radius_8a minus sequence_window_8 leave-one-out neighbor-label AUPRC
statistics.secondary_comparison: within-complex spatial_radius_16a minus spatial_radius_8a leave-one-out neighbor-label AUPRC

interpretation_guardrail: Neighbor labels are deliberately used to measure topology. The resulting AUPRC is a label-autocorrelation diagnostic, not predictive model performance.
promotion_rule: A new multi-relation architecture may be implemented only as an isolated exploratory condition. The diagnostic may choose its graph scales but cannot alter the frozen confirmatory matrix or authorize test opening.
claim_boundary: AsEP validation-label topology analysis only. No official test, frozen test, external score, checkpoint selection, benchmark improvement, or state-of-the-art claim is authorized.
